guard_streams.write_limit: No second task, owner takeover or parallel runner is permitted.

The source snapshot remains exact_rows_returned zero and source_scan_complete remains false.

facts.detail: Coverage reports predicted local 4G or 5G availability, separating indoor and outdoor conditions and good versus variable signal.
Performance reports the likelihood that measurements can support video streaming or a video call in the local postal geography.

guard_streams.write_limit: Coverage prediction and performance experience are different outputs and cannot be merged into fixed-broadband fields.

facts.detail: The newer checker provides local coverage information at 50 metre squares where the source data supports that resolution.
The earlier checker used 100 metre squares throughout, so products from different vintages must retain their declared resolution.

guard_streams.write_limit: A mobile grid square is not a fixed postcode or parcel observation.

guard_streams.source: Map Your Mobile checker update footnotes

facts.detail: Vodafone predictions were still supplied at 100 metre resolution for the documented update.
Ofcom scaled those 100 metre inputs to 50 metre pixels for consistent nationwide calculations until native 50 metre data became available.

guard_streams.write_limit: Rescaling does not increase the underlying spatial evidence or create parcel precision.

facts.detail: The checker distinguishes good outdoor, variable outdoor and poor-to-no outdoor coverage.
Indoor categories distinguish good versus variable in-home expectations and are explicitly presented as guidance.

guard_streams.write_limit: Consumer display classes are not exact fixed-line availability percentages.

facts.detail: Ofcom states there is no signal-strength threshold that guarantees connectivity 100 percent of the time.
Predicted coverage cannot be 100 percent accurate because service depends on additional local and network conditions.

guard_streams.write_limit: Prediction confidence must not be relabelled as parcel certainty.

facts.detail: The documented performance score uses the share of successful connections achieving 5 Mbit/s download.
That share is used as an indicator of the probability of obtaining a connection suitable for a more reliable service.

guard_streams.write_limit: A mobile 5 Mbit/s experience threshold is not a fixed-broadband coverage threshold.

guard_streams.source: Map Your Mobile launch and 2026 milestone

facts.detail: The performance component uses crowdsourced Opensignal measurements based on real mobile-user experience.
The launch documentation describes independent analysis of more than 20 million tests across the UK.

guard_streams.write_limit: Crowdsourced test volume cannot establish complete or unbiased parcel coverage.

facts.detail: Performance measurements are collected from smartphones every day under normal-use conditions.
The measurement population includes both indoor and outdoor observations to reflect typical user behaviour.

guard_streams.write_limit: Opportunistic mobile samples are not controlled fixed-line measurements.

facts.detail: Performance is normally reported at postal-district level because that is generally the smallest area with enough measurements for statistical confidence.
When a district lacks sufficient samples, the checker can use the wider parent postal area under the same reporting rules.

guard_streams.write_limit: District or postal-area fallback averages must not be assigned to an individual postcode or parcel.

facts.detail: A district performance display requires enough measurements for all four main mobile networks to pass the statistical-confidence threshold.
The checker displays N/A when that threshold is not met rather than estimating a score.

guard_streams.write_limit: Insufficient samples must remain unknown rather than inferred.

facts.detail: Performance percentages are calculated from the most recent 12 months of data available at the upload date.
Ofcom aims to upload refreshed performance data each quarter.

guard_streams.write_limit: A rolling mobile-performance window is not the January 2026 fixed-coverage snapshot.

facts.detail: Coverage uses operator predictions while performance uses crowdsourced measurements, so the outputs can legitimately differ.
A district may show reasonable performance while a specific spot lacks coverage; Ofcom advises using the coverage result for the spot-location expectation.

guard_streams.write_limit: District performance cannot override a location-specific coverage result.
